title: Data Pipeline Contract Lab
briefing: Design a versioned training-data contract and try to break it with late data, duplicates, leakage, and a changed production population.
objectives: Define row grain, keys, event time, labels, and validation boundaries.
Choose a split strategy that represents deployment.
Preserve lineage from source through training dataset.

prediction.prompt: Which split is safest when multiple records from one user occur over time and deployment predicts future behavior?

options.label: Time-aware split with entity leakage controls

steps.title: Specify the contract
steps.instructions: Define grain, key, event time, label availability, types, missingness rules, and five domain invariants for a concrete dataset.

steps.title: Defend the split
steps.instructions: Describe production timing and entity relationships, choose a split, and identify two leakage paths the split must prevent.

steps.title: Build lineage
steps.instructions: Record source version, extraction window, transformation revision, parameters, output identifier, and downstream model run.

steps.title: Inject a failure
steps.instructions: Simulate late labels, duplicate events, or a category change and decide whether to reject, quarantine, warn, or rebuild.

evidenceChecklist.label: Row grain and keys are unambiguous
Split strategy addresses time and entity leakage
A model run can be traced to a dataset and transformation revision

reflectionPrompts: Which validation protects correctness, and which only signals drift?
How would a corrected historical label propagate to trained artifacts?
extensionChallenge: Add an online feature path and define a measurable offline-online skew check plus an incident response.
